result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the fear of being wrong.

Not just the fear of failure, but the deep, paralyzing fear of being *wrong*—of having to admit that what you believed, what you built, what you stood for, might not be true. Because that fear is the root of so much: the resistance to new ideas, the cruelty of dogma, the way we cling to lies when the truth is too heavy to bear.

If we could unlearn that fear, we could finally ask better questions. We could listen instead of defend. We could change our minds without shame. And maybe, just maybe, we could build something real—something that lasts—not because it’s perfect, but because it’s honest.
